body:
## Problem

A person who rates a PostHog Slack answer on a Codex run sends a rating that points at nothing, so nobody can open the turn and see what the agent did.

- The Claude CLI mints a `traceparent` per user turn, and [ai-gateway#496](https://github.com/PostHog/ai-gateway/pull/496) taught the gateway to read it, so a Claude turn's generations share one `$ai_trace_id`.
- Codex sends no trace header, so the gateway falls through to stamping a fresh id per request.
- A Codex run's generations therefore each sit alone in a trace of one, and AI observability has no turn to show.

## Changes

- A rating on a Codex turn now resolves to that turn, and the turn's generations appear as one trace.
- The agent-server sets `X-PostHog-Trace-Id` to the run id on the Codex gateway headers.
- The agent-server then reports that run id as the turn's trace id on every path a rating can arrive by: the command result the Slack relay reads, the direct relay, and the turn-complete event the agent-design stream reads.
- The Codex adapter mints its own turn-complete event and reports no trace id, so the server fills it in on the way through.
- Claude keeps its own per-turn ids. That header outranks `traceparent`, so setting it for Claude would replace them with one id for the whole run.
- Nothing changes in the app UI. The effect lands in AI observability and on the rating.

The id is resolved next to the stamp rather than in the Temporal activity that posts the reply. The activity would have to infer it from the run's `runtime_adapter`, and a Codex run with no `AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN` falls back to the Python gateway and carries no stamp, so the inferred id would point a rating at a trace with no generations.

The obvious alternative is a Codex-side per-turn hook mirroring Claude's `traceparent-hook`. Codex accepts gateway headers only at process spawn, through `model_providers.posthog.http_headers`, so it has no per-turn seam. `configureEnvironment` runs once per run, which makes the run the finest granularity available, and the run is the unit a Slack rating already refers to.

## How did you test this code?

- `withTurnTraceId` covers the turn-complete event, 3 cases. It catches the two ways the fallback goes wrong: overwriting a trace id the adapter reported, and naming a run that no header stamped.
- One case in `agent-server.configure-environment.test.ts` covers the header. It catches the header landing on a Claude run, which would replace the CLI's per-turn ids.
- Not run: the desktop Playwright suite. Three cases in `agent-server.test.ts` fail in this sandbox for reasons outside this change: the sandbox git guard blocks the fixture's `git commit`, and the sandbox's own agent instructions reach the built system prompt.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

The change came out of reading eight weeks of `slack_app` traces: Codex-adapter runs group at zero while Claude-adapter runs group as intended since ai-gateway#496, which pointed at the missing header rather than at the gateway.

An earlier revision resolved the id in `forward_pending_message`, a Temporal activity under `products/tasks/`. Three reviewers found the same gap, on the paths that activity never reaches. The resolution moved into the agent-server and the `products/tasks/` half came out, which also drops the desktop and backend coupling this PR carried.

Skills invoked: `posthog-desktop`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: skipped. The CLI is installed but signed out, and signing in opens a browser. `auto_review` posts a review on each push.

No customer data, session links, or internal material appear in this branch. The trace-grouping observation is about PostHog's own agent behaviour, and the test fixtures are invented.
title: fix(tasks): give a codex turn one trace id
